title.en: World Desk
title.zh: 全球焦点

strap.en: A fast view of global affairs, conflict, diplomacy, and human need.

title.en: Datacentres facing increase in global climate-related legal cases, report finds
title.zh: 报告发现数据中心面临全球气候相关法律案件增多

summary.en: A report by the London School of Economics indicates a global rise in climate-related legal cases against datacentres and AI companies. These lawsuits are primarily linked to concerns over energy consumption, water usage, and air pollution caused by the proliferation of these technologies.
summary.zh: 伦敦经济学院的一份报告指出，全球范围内针对数据中心和人工智能公司的气候相关法律案件正在增加。这些诉讼主要与这些技术扩散所造成的能源消耗、水资源使用和空气污染问题有关。

body.en: LSE analysis highlights litigation linked to energy sources, water consumption and air pollution The proliferation of datacentres and AI is increasingly at the forefront of environmental litigation around the world from Chile to Ireland, a report has found. In an analysis of about 3,600 climate-related lawsuits filed since 2015, the latest annual review of climate litigation by the London School of Economics (LSE) found a growing number of cases challenging the energy sources, water consumption and air pollution of datacentres, all of which have related climate implications. Continue reading...
body.zh: 伦敦证券交易所的分析强调了与能源、水消耗和空气污染相关的诉讼 一份报告发现，从智利到爱尔兰，数据中心和人工智能的激增日益成为世界各地环境诉讼的前沿。伦敦经济学院 (LSE) 最新的气候诉讼年度审查对 2015 年以来提起的约 3,600 起气候相关诉讼进行了分析，发现越来越多的案件挑战数据中心的能源、水消耗和空气污染，所有这些都与气候影响有关。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The increasing legal challenges against datacentres highlight our collective responsibility to care for the Earth, which ultimately belongs to Yahweh. As technology advances, we are called to consider its environmental impact and ensure our innovations serve creation, not harm it.
reflection.zh: 针对数据中心的法律挑战日益增多，凸显了我们对地球的共同责任，因为地球最终属于雅伟。随着科技进步，我们蒙召思考其对环境的影响，并确保我们的创新是服务而非损害受造界。

verse.textEn: The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.
verse.textZh: 地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。

title.en: Europe braced for another day of extreme heat as warnings issued across UK, France and Italy – live
title.zh: 欧洲多国严阵以待，应对又一个极端高温日，英法意发布预警

summary.en: Europe is preparing for another day of extreme heat, with warnings issued across the UK, France, and Italy. In the UK, South East Water has implemented a temporary hosepipe ban in Kent due to the strain on water supplies from the ongoing heatwave, which is expected to reach 33C.
summary.zh: 欧洲正准备迎接又一个极端高温日，英国、法国和意大利都发布了高温预警。在英国，由于持续热浪导致水资源供应紧张，预计气温将达到33摄氏度，东南水务公司已在肯特郡实施了临时软管禁令。

body.en: UK June heat record could be broken for the second consecutive day Farryn Stock Over in the UK, South East Water has announced a temporary hosepipe ban in Kent amid growing strain from the ongoing heatwave (31C today, 33C tomorrow). “To safeguard that shared supply and prevent any homes from facing a sudden loss of water, we sadly need to ask our communities to not use their hosepipes immediately. We are deeply sorry for the disruption this causes, and we are incredibly grateful to everyone helping us protect Kent’s water.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 英国 6 月高温记录可能连续第二天被打破 英国法林斯托克 (Farryn Stock) 在英国，由于持续的热浪（今天 31 摄氏度，明天 33 摄氏度）带来的压力越来越大，东南水务公司宣布在肯特郡实施临时软管禁令。 “为了保障共享供应并防止任何家庭面临突然断水的情况，我们遗憾地需要要求我们的社区不要立即使用他们的软管。我们对由此造成的破坏深表歉意，我们非常感谢每个帮助我们保护肯特郡水的人。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: The widespread heatwave and resulting water restrictions remind us of our role as stewards of creation. Yahweh placed humanity in the garden to tend and keep it, a call to responsible care for the earth and its precious resources. In times of environmental strain, this ancient mandate becomes especially urgent, prompting us to consider how we manage what...
reflection.zh: 欧洲多地持续高温，水资源面临压力，这提醒我们作为受造物的管家所肩负的责任。雅伟将人类安置在伊甸园中，吩咐他们修理看守，这是对地球及其宝贵资源负责任的呼召。在环境面临压力时，这一古老的使命变得尤为紧迫，促使我们思考如何管理所托付的一切。

verse.textEn: Yahweh God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.
verse.textZh: 雅伟神将那人安置在伊甸园，使他修理看守。

title.en: US renters call for action to combat surge of ‘take it or leave it’ apartment fees
title.zh: 美国租户呼吁采取行动，打击公寓“不接受就作罢”式收费的激增

summary.en: Renters across the US are advocating for stronger regulations to combat a rise in what they describe as unfair, non-negotiable apartment fees. Industry representatives, however, contend that such policies could restrict the effective use of these charges.
summary.zh: 美国各地的租户呼吁制定更严格的法规，以打击他们所称的不公平、不可协商的公寓附加费激增的现象。然而，行业代表辩称，此类政策可能会限制这些收费的“有效使用”。

body.en: Tenants push for tougher rules against unfair add-on charges. Industry players argue against policies that they say could limit the ‘effective use of fees’ ‘Extremely overwhelmed’: apartment renters face rising tide of fees Across the US, many renters are calling for national action to stem add-on charges that spike their housing costs and increase their risk of eviction. “The rental housing market is one where consumers have little power,” Farah Momin, a renter in Seattle, told the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) in April. “Landlords can impose fees through take-it-or-leave-it lease terms, and the cost/disruption of moving means that tenants may absorb unfair charges rather than leave. Federal baseline protections are needed to level this playing field.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 租户推动制定更严格的规则来打击不公平的附加费用。业内人士反对他们认为可能限制“费用有效使用”的政策“不堪重负”：公寓租户面临费用上涨的浪潮在美国各地，许多租户呼吁采取国家行动，阻止附加费用飙升，增加他们的住房成本并增加被驱逐的风险。 “租赁住房市场是消费者几乎没有权力的市场，”西雅图的一名租户法拉·莫明 (Farah Momin) 四月份告诉联邦贸易委员会 (FTC)。 “房东可以通过要么接受要么离开的租赁条款来收取费用，而搬家的成本/中断意味着租户可能会承担不公平的费用而不是离开。需要联邦基线保护来公平竞争。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for fair housing practices reminds us that Yahweh values integrity in all transactions. When renters face "take it or leave it" fees, it highlights the need for just and transparent dealings in commerce. Yahweh delights in honest measures that ensure fairness for everyone, especially those seeking a home.
reflection.zh: 租户对公平住房实践的呼吁提醒我们，雅伟看重所有交易中的诚信。当租户面临“不接受就作罢”的费用时，这突显了商业往来中需要公正和透明。雅伟喜悦诚实的衡量，确保每个人，特别是那些寻求居所的人，都能获得公平。

verse.textEn: Yahweh detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him.
verse.textZh: 诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶；公平的法码为他所喜悦。

title.en: Louisiana sheriff retires after pleading guilty to beating podcaster who often criticized him
title.zh: 路易斯安那州警长在承认殴打批评他的播客主持人后退休

summary.en: A Louisiana sheriff has retired as part of a plea deal after admitting to beating a podcaster who had been critical of him. The sheriff, who held a prominent political office for a decade, pleaded guilty to the assault.
summary.zh: 路易斯安那州的一名警长在承认殴打一名经常批评他的播客主持人后，作为认罪协议的一部分宣布退休。这位在新奥尔良郊区担任了十年重要政治职务的警长，已对此次袭击认罪。

body.en: Randy Smith’s resignation was part of plea deal after attack on podcaster Bobby Couvillion at a Madisonville restaurant A suburban New Orleans sheriff who had held one of his community’s most prominent political offices for a decade has retired shortly after pleading guilty to battering a podcaster who often criticized him. Randy Smith, 61, also agreed to serve more than a year of probation after admitting to a late May beating at a steakhouse where he had bought 18 alcoholic beverages on his tab on a Friday afternoon – which all but halted his four-decade policing career. Continue reading...
body.zh: 兰迪·史密斯（Randy Smith）的辞职是在麦迪逊维尔一家餐厅袭击播客鲍比·库维利恩（Bobby Couvillion）后认罪协议的一部分。新奥尔良郊区的一名警长十年来担任社区最著名的政治职务之一，在承认殴打一名经常批评他的播客的罪名后不久就退休了。 61 岁的兰迪·史密斯 (Randy Smith) 也同意服刑一年多，他承认自己在 5 月下旬的一个周五下午在一家牛排馆遭到殴打，并在账单上购买了 18 种酒精饮料，这几乎终止了他 40 年的警察生涯。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story reminds us that those in positions of authority are called to uphold justice and integrity. Proverbs 16:12 states that "Righteous rule detests wrongdoing, for a throne is established through righteousness." When leaders abuse their power, it undermines the very foundation of their office and the trust placed in them by the community.
reflection.zh: 这个故事提醒我们，身居高位者蒙召维护公义和正直。箴言16:12说：“君王以行恶为可憎，因国位是靠公义坚立。”当领袖滥用权力时，就会动摇其职位的根基，并辜负社区对他们的信任。

verse.textEn: Kings detest wrongdoing, for a throne is established through righteousness.
verse.textZh: 作恶为王所憎恶，因国位是靠公义坚立。

title.zh: 检查人员称，诺丁汉国民医疗服务体系信任太平间的尸体处于“严重恶化”状态

summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Human Tissue Authority says bodies not transferred to freezer in time due to insufficient storage needs Bodies in the mortuary at the NHS trust at the centre of the health services biggest ever maternity care scandal were found in a state of “advanced deterioration” due to not being transferred to a freezer in time, inspectors have said. Human Tissue Authority (HTA) inspectors who visited Nottingham university hospitals NHS trust in March discovered eight bodies in a state of advanced decomposition due to not being transferred to a freezer within a sufficient timeframe. Continue reading...
body.zh: 人体组织管理局表示，由于存储需求不足，尸体没有及时转移到冰箱检查人员表示，由于没有及时转移到冰箱，尸体在NHS信托太平间被发现处于“严重恶化”状态。人体组织管理局（HTA）检查人员三月份访问了诺丁汉大学医院 NHS 信托基金，发现了八具处于严重腐烂状态的尸体，原因是没有在足够的时间内转移到冰箱中。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to compassion for vulnerable people. Galatians 6:2 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with practical compassion and welcome, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到对脆弱群体的怜悯。Galatians 6:2提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以具体的怜悯与接纳来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: How countries live with earthquakes and build resilience
title.zh: 各国如何与地震共存并建立韧性

summary.en: The article explores how various countries have developed strategies, innovations, and determination to mitigate the risks associated with earthquakes, demonstrating that living in earthquake-prone regions does not necessitate constant fear. It highlights successful approaches to preparation and resilience that save...
summary.zh: 这篇文章探讨了各国如何通过策略、创新和决心来减轻地震带来的风险，表明生活在地震多发区并不意味着必须生活在恐惧中。文章重点介绍了成功应对地震并挽救生命的准备和韧性方法。

body.en:
Earthquakes are a fact of nature, but living with earthquakes doesn't have to mean living in fear. DW takes a closer look at some countries showing how preparation, innovation and determination can save lives.

Two major earthquakes struck central Venezuela seconds apart on Wednesday , one with a magnitude 7.2 and the other with a magnitude 7.5. At least 32 people have been killed, and hundreds injured.

Extensive damage was reported in the capital, Caracas, and the nearby state of La Guaira.

Strong earthquakes are unusual in Venezuela, even though it sits near multiple fault lines along the South American and Caribbean tectonic plates. Other countries on the Pacific coast, including Mexico, Chile and the western edge of the United States, are positioned along the seismically active tectonic belt known as the Ring of Fire, responsible for about 90% of the world's earthquakes .

However, several countries that once faced devastating losses have proven that living with earthquakes doesn't have to mean living in fear. Their experiences show that resilience isn't just about surviving the next earthquake but about building systems that protect lives before the ground begins to shake.

Japan  is one of the world's most earthquake-prone countries. Over decades, it has transformed vulnerability into resilience, thanks to a mix of technology, architecture and public preparedness.

A key pillar is the Earthquake Early Warning system, operated by the Japan Meteorological Agency. Since 2007, this system has used over a thousand seismic sensors to detect the first, weaker P-waves (primary waves) and send alerts through phones, TV, radio and loudspeakers, giving people critical seconds before stronger shaking begins.

Japan's resilience has also been built into its cities. After the Great Kanto Earthquake of 1923, building codes were strengthened, though it took some time.

A major shift came in 1981, when new regulations (Shin-Taishin) required all new constructions to meet stricter seismic standards. Many essential facilities, such as hospitals and government centers, now use seismic isolation systems — engineering solutions that allow structures to sway and to absorb, rather than resist, energy.

Miho Mazereeuw, an associate professor at Massachusetts Institute of Technology and director of the Urban Risk Lab, explained this approach to CNN after the 2024 Noto Peninsula earthquake. "Conceptually, it all comes back to the idea that, rather than resisting the movement of the Earth, you let the building move with it," she said, explaining how preparedness is part of everyday life in Japan.

Earthquake drills start from a young age, evacuation routes are clearly marked and parks and schoolyards...
body.zh: 地震是自然现象，但与地震共存并不一定意味着生活在恐惧之中。德国之声仔细研究了一些国家，展示了准备、创新和决心如何能够拯救生命。 周三，委内瑞拉中部发生了两次大地震，两次地震相隔几秒，一次为 7.2 级，另一次为 7.5 级。至少32人死亡，数百人受伤。 据报道，首都加拉加斯和附近的拉瓜伊拉州遭受了严重破坏。 尽管委内瑞拉位于南美和加勒比板块的多条断层线附近，但强烈地震在委内瑞拉并不常见。太平洋沿岸的其他国家，包括墨西哥、智利和美国西部边缘，都位于被称为“火环”的地震活跃构造带上，世界上约 90% 的地震是由该构造带造成的。 然而，一些曾经遭受毁灭性损失的国家已经证明，生活在地震中并不一定意味着生活在恐惧之中。他们的经验表明，复原力不仅仅是在下一次地震中幸存下来，而是在地面开始摇晃之前建立保护生命的系统。 日本是世界上地震最频繁的国家之一。几十年来，得益于技术、架构和公众准备的结合，它已将脆弱性转化为韧性。 一个关键支柱是由日本气象厅运营的地震早期预警系统。自 2007 年以来，该系统已使用超过 1000 个地震传感器来检测第一个较弱的 P 波（主波），并通过电话、电视、收音机和扬声器发送警报，在更强的震动开始之前为人们提供关键的几秒钟时间。 日本的韧性也体现在其城市中。 1923 年关东大地震后，建筑规范得到加强，但花了一些时间。 1981 年发生了重大转变，当时新法规（Shin-Taishin）要求所有新建建筑满足更严格的抗震标准。许多重要设施，例如医院和政府中心，现在都使用隔震系统，这种工程解决方案允许结构摇摆并吸收而不是抵抗能量。 麻省理工学院副教授兼城市风险实验室主任 Miho Mazereeuw 在 2024 年能登半岛地震后向 CNN 解释了这种方法。 “从概念上讲，这一切都回到了这样一个想法，即不是抵抗地球的运动，而是让建筑物随之移动，”她说，并解释了备灾如何成为日本日常生活的一部分。 地震演习从小就开始，疏散路线有清晰的标记，公园和校园……

reflection.en: Natural disasters like earthquakes remind us of the fragility of life and the power of creation. Yet, as this report shows, human ingenuity and collective effort can transform suffering into perseverance, building resilience and hope for the future. Yahweh's presence can strengthen communities to face these challenges with courage and determination.
reflection.zh: 地震等自然灾害提醒我们生命的脆弱和创造的巨大力量。然而，正如这篇报道所示，人类的智慧和集体努力能将苦难转化为坚韧，为未来建立韧性和希望。雅伟的同在能加添社区的力量，使其以勇气和决心面对这些挑战。

verse.textEn: We also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.
verse.textZh: 就是在患难中也是欢欢喜喜的；因为知道患难生忍耐，忍耐生老练，老练生盼望。

title.en: Police seal off key roads in Nairobi as Kenya braces for Gen Z protests
title.zh: 肯尼亚为 Z 世代抗议做好准备，警方封锁了内罗毕的主要道路

summary.en: Protesters demand justice for more than 80 people killed during the 2024 demonstrations and last year's anniversary protests.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Police in Kenya have sealed off key roads leading into central Nairobi ahead of planned nationwide protests marking two years since the deadly Gen-Z-led anti-government demonstrations.

Thousands of Kenyans protested against proposed tax hikes in June 2024, culminating in the storming of parliament and the eventual withdrawal of the controversial finance bill.

Protesters say they are demanding justice for more than 80 people killed and dozens more injured during the 2024 anti-tax demonstrations and last year's anniversary protests.

The planned protests, largely mobilised through social media platforms, are expected to take place in major towns including Nairobi, Mombasa and parts of central Kenya.

Security agencies have heightened surveillance in major urban centres ahead of the protests, with police expected to maintain a heavy presence in Nairobi and strategic installations.

Police officers on horseback have been dispersing crowds trying to gather along Nairobi streets.

Footage from a local TV station shows flames and smoke rising in the Githurai area near Nairobi, as protesters lit fires during clashes with police.

Police officers were also seen firing tear gas to disperse crowds gathered in the area. Several people have been arrested by anti-riot police in Nairobi, while trying to access the city.

Deputy police chief Gilbert Masengeli said roadblocks were mounted to ensure no criminals or weapons entered the city, adding that the country remained calm, with citizens going about their daily activities without disruption.

"There are no blocked roads. We are just ensuring the safety of Kenyans. We are just checking if they are carrying weapons," said Masengeli.

"I am grateful because there are no vehicles being burnt and people are going about their work," he added.

Some parents who lost children during the 2024 protests have asked the government to allow them to peacefully remember their loved ones.

"We don't want tear gas and running battles in the streets. We are too old for that," one of the parents told journalists in Nairobi.

Opposition leaders led by Kalonzo Musyoka, Martha Karua and Eugene Wamalwa joined families of the victims to lay wreath at parliament in honour of those who died during the 2024 demonstations.

Early on Thursday, police mounted roadblocks along the Thika Super Highway, Mombasa Road, the Nairobi-Namanga Highway in Athi River, Kenyatta Avenue, Waiyaki Way, Jogoo Road, and other major routes, preventing motorists and pedestrians from accessing the city centre.

Authorities have urged protesters to remain peaceful and avoid acts of violence, looting, or destruction of property.

title.en: Kenya's Gen Z protests still echo two years on
title.zh: 肯尼亚Z世代抗议两年后仍在回响

summary.en: Two years after youth-led protests in Kenya, activists state that the underlying issues remain unresolved. The decentralized Gen Z movement continues to influence politics, advocate for justice, and challenge existing power structures.
summary.zh: 肯尼亚青年主导的抗议活动两年后，活动人士表示问题仍未解决。这个去中心化的Z世代运动继续影响政治，要求伸张正义，并挑战权力。

body.en:
Two years after youth-led protests shook Kenya, activists say the issues remain unresolved. As Gen Z marks the anniversary, the decentralized movement continues to shape politics, demand justice, and challenge power.

Kenya's anti-riot police were out in full force in the capital, Nairobi, on Thursday, two years after Gen Z protesters breached the grounds of Kenya's parliament during demonstrations against the Finance Bill 2024.

For many young Kenyans, June 25 is no longer just a protest date ; it has become a symbol of resistance against police brutality , economic hardship and what activists see as a growing gap between leaders and citizens. Many young Kenyans say little has fundamentally changed. Youth unemployment, rising cost of living and concerns over governance continue to resonate across the same generation that first mobilized online and poured into the streets.

"June 25th is a reminder of what this regime is all about," Faith Njeri, a university student in Nairobi, told DW. "It is a reminder of when you guys lost legitimacy to the people of Kenya … because of just simply saying no to the Finance Bill."

Others emphasized the importance of commemoration."Thursday is our greatest day that is about to happen," said youth activist Brian Otieno. "Celebrate the life of the comrades who died … We are coming with flowers. So your government should prepare to give us security."

Digital activism continues to play a crucial role in the Gen Z-led protests. "Kenyans we have decided we are all changing our profile pictures to Rex and the other heroes we lost… Everyone we've lost to police brutality," said Mercy Wanjiru. "You cannot kill us and lead us."

For some, remembrance is also about restoring names that risk being forgotten. "We are in that dark month … Rex Masai, Denzel Omondi, Eric Shieni, David Chege, Erickson Mutisya… and the many who disappeared," businessman Kevin Mwangi, told DW. At least 60 deaths were recorded during the protests, according to the government-mandated Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR). Rex Masai , a 29-year-old activist was the first fatality of the June 2024 anti-Finance Bill protests.

Unlike earlier  protest waves in Kenya , which often revolved around political parties or established civil society actors, the anti-Finance Bill demonstrations were markedly decentralized. Organizing largely unfolded online, through social media platforms and loosely connected local networks.

Beatrice Waithera, national leader of the Red Vest Movement, told DW this approach was partly a response to increasing scrutiny of public gatherings. body.zh: 年轻人领导的抗议活动震撼了肯尼亚两年后，活动人士表示这些问题仍未得到解决。在 Z 世代纪念周年之际，去中心化运动继续塑造政治、要求正义并挑战权力。 周四，Z 世代抗议者在反对《2024 年金融法案》的示威活动中冲进肯尼亚议会场地，两年后，肯尼亚首都内罗毕全力出动防暴警察。 对于许多肯尼亚年轻人来说，6月25日不再只是一个抗议的日子；它已成为抵抗警察暴行、经济困难以及活动人士所认为的领导人与公民之间日益扩大的差距的象征。许多肯尼亚年轻人表示，几乎没有什么根本改变。青年失业、生活成本上升以及对治理的担忧继续在最先在网上动员起来并涌上街头的同一代人中引起共鸣。 “6月25日提醒我们这个政权的本质，”内罗毕的大学生费思·恩杰里(Faith Njeri)告诉德国之声。 “这提醒人们，你们在肯尼亚人民面前失去了合法性……因为只是对财政法案说不。” 其他人则强调了纪念活动的重要性。“星期四是我们即将发生的最伟大的一天，”青年活动家布莱恩·奥蒂诺 (Brian Otieno) 说。 “庆祝逝去战友的生命……我们带着鲜花而来。所以你们的政府应该准备好为我们提供安全保障。” 数字激进主义继续在 Z 世代领导的抗议活动中发挥至关重要的作用。 “肯尼亚人，我们决定将我们的个人资料照片全部改为雷克斯和我们失去的其他英雄......我们在警察暴行中失去的每个人，”默西·万吉鲁说。 “你不能杀死我们并领导我们。” 对于一些人来说，纪念还在于恢复可能被遗忘的名字。商人凯文·姆旺吉（Kevin Mwangi）告诉德国之声：“我们正处于那个黑暗的月份……雷克斯·马赛（Rex Masai）、丹泽尔·奥蒙迪（Denzel Omondi）、埃里克·谢尼（Eric Shieni）、大卫·切格（David Chege）、埃里克森·穆蒂西亚（Erickson Mutisya）……以及许多失踪的人。”据政府授权的肯尼亚国家人权委员会 (KNCHR) 称，抗议期间至少有 60 人死亡。 29 岁的活动家雷克斯·马赛 (Rex Masai) 是 2024 年 6 月反金融法案抗议活动中的第一名死亡者。 与肯尼亚早期的抗议浪潮通常围绕政党或民间社会参与者不同，反金融法案的示威活动明显是分散的。组织活动主要通过社交媒体平台和松散连接的本地网络在网上进行。 红背心运动全国领导人比阿特丽斯·维瑟拉(Beatrice Waitera)告诉德国之声，这种做法在一定程度上是为了应对公众集会日益严格的审查。 “我们必须谨慎地动员自己，就像威廉·鲁托总统必须进入 X（以前的 Twitter）上的一个空间，尝试与我们交谈一样，”...

title.en: 'I thought I was going to die' - Venezuelans describe earthquake panic
title.zh: “我以为我要死了”——委内瑞拉人描述地震恐慌

summary.en: An earthquake struck Caracas, Venezuela, causing buildings to flatten. Voices were heard calling from the rubble, as residents described experiencing panic during the event.
summary.zh: 委内瑞拉首都加拉加斯发生地震，导致建筑物倒塌。有居民描述在地震中感到恐慌，废墟中传出呼救声。

body.en:
When the ground beneath Venezuela started violently rocking on Wednesday evening, Verónica feared the walls of her Caracas apartment would bury her.

She was at home celebrating a national holiday with her mother when tremors from two earthquakes hit the city, seconds apart, around 18:00 local time (22:00 GMT): the first at a magnitude of 7.2 and the second at 7.5.

More than 30 people have been confirmed dead so far and hundreds more are injured - but authorities have warned they have not even begun to gauge the losses in some of the hardest hit areas.

Debris is strewn around the streets of Caracas, Venezuela's capital, as rescuers dig through the wreckage of collapsed buildings to locate survivors. In some footage, people can be heard calling for help.

Across other affected parts of Venezeula, a picture of the damage is still emerging as power and internet outages add to the chaos.

As night fell, dazed locals - many rendered functionally homeless - milled the streets, waiting for news on their homes or loved ones.

Verónica is the sister of BBC Mundo's Valentina Oropeza - and the journalist spent hours trying to track down her family after the quakes.

Valentina's phone had pinged with a breathy voice message from Verónica describing the "awful" tremors in real time, their mother's voice distant in the background. Then radio silence.

Panicked, Valentina began asking her network for help to contact the pair as images of crushed buildings on their street began filling her phone.

When she finally was able to reach them, Verónica confirmed she and her mother were safe but said she has likely lost her home.

This is not the first time the Venezuelan capital has been hit by a major earthquake.

In 1967, a 6.6-magnitude quake struck Caracas and killed more than 200 people, destroying buildings in Palos Grandes and the upper-class area of Altamira.

But the ones on Wednesday felt worse - much longer and more intense, said Valentina's mother.

"I never thought we would experience something like this," she said, audibly shaken.

Coro Martinez, a resident in eastern Caracas, told Reuters news agency the same.

"There was a very loud crash. Things fell in the house, jugs inside the refrigerator."

BBC Mundo journalist Nicole Kolster saw the windows of her seventh storey apartment in Palos Grandes, a prime district in central Caracas, begin to shake and and had just moments to shelter.

"The only thing I could think to do was to get between the front door and a stone wall... to try to protect myself."

Evacuating to the street, she said she could hear voices coming from mountains of rubble. Survivors - so rushed to flee they had not paused to put on shoes - were hugging and crying.

title.en: Trump asks Congress for billions for Iran war, after tension with Republicans
title.zh: 在与共和党关系紧张后，特朗普要求国会为伊朗战争提供数十亿美元

summary.en: But the budget faces an uphill battle as the president spars with some members of his own party over the issue.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The White House has asked lawmakers to approve $87.6bn (£66.5bn), mostly for "urgent needs" connected with the US war on Iran, a day after Congress passed a resolution rebuking the military action.

The bulk of the funding - $67bn - is for the US Department of Defence, the White House said.

But the proposal faces an uphill battle in Congress. The Iran conflict is unpopular with voters ahead of the US midterm elections in November, though a ceasefire is currently in effect.

US President Donald Trump has also found himself at odds with some members of his Republican Party over the issue of Iran, and is alleged to have ended up in an angry exchange with one senator on Wednesday.

That senator, Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, was one of a handful of Republicans who defied the president on Tuesday by voting to pass a measure demanding that he halt the war or seek congressional approval before continuing military action.

Cassidy fell back in line after his alleged sparring with the president, and after receiving assurances from members of Trump's administration. He and others went on to vote down another similar measure in the Senate late on Wednesday.

The White House Office of Management and Budget sent the formal request for the funds on Wednesday in a letter to House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson.

"Most of this request will address urgent needs related to Operation Epic Fury (OEF)," says the letter, referring to the Iran war.

The request includes $21bn for munitions, $17.3bn for operational costs and $12.1bn for classified programmes. It also asks for about $300m to bolster security at US embassies and diplomatic outposts in the Middle East and South Asia after some of them came under attack earlier in the war.

The other requested money would be for unrelated measures, including $11bn for US farmers and $1.4bn to tackle the Ebola outbreak in Central Africa.

Washington and Tehran are currently observing a ceasefire in the war, but the White House budget office letter notes that the Pentagon needs to "rebuild stocks" after its military strikes.

A peace plan was last week agreed between Trump and Iran, but dissident voices within the Republican Party have voiced scepticism about it.

The meeting between the president and senators on Wednesday was said to have been tense after Trump abruptly called off a signing ceremony for a housing bill that had bipartisan support.

At the lunch on Capitol Hill, Trump went on to complain about the measure that was passed the previous evening, when the Republican-controlled Senate narrowly voted to call for a restriction on his war powers.

Despite being largely symbolic, the measure was the first resolution of its kind to clear Congress that demanded a president to end a military action.

title.en: Find out which university degrees could earn you most across your lifetime
title.zh: 了解哪些大学学位能让你一生赚得最多

summary.en: New data indicates which university degrees offer the highest and lowest financial returns over a lifetime.
summary.zh: 新数据显示，哪些大学学位在一生中能带来最高和最低的经济回报。

body.en:
Although a university degree is widely understood to lead to better earnings over a lifetime, new research suggests it can vary significantly depending on which course you do.

You can use our look-up tool below to check your chosen subject and find out how much more - or less - graduates can earn compared with non-graduates.

On average, graduates picking medicine can earn up to £400,000 more over their lifetime compared to non-graduates, research by the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) suggests.

Economics could also earn graduates significantly more but other subjects, including creative arts, philosophy and languages, offer little to negative financial return when compared to the earnings of someone similar without a degree, the research suggests.

The Department for Education (DfE) says it will cap numbers on courses with poorest returns, and will consult on the introduction of minimum English language requirements.

The data suggests the average graduate earns around £100,000 more over their lifetime than non-graduate counterparts, even after taxes and student loan repayments.

While there are significant financial benefits to undergraduate degrees on average, the data suggests a quarter of graduates can expect to be financially worse off over their lifetime as a result of going to university.

One in ten male graduates will potentially be more than £90,000 worse off than they otherwise would have been.

For students who continued in education post-16, but had relatively low GCSE grades, the data reflects that they can expect their lifetime take-home pay to be £53,000 higher on average than peers with similar grades who did not attend university.

However, among graduate men with low prior attainment, around four in 10 can expect to be worse-off financially over their lifetimes than if they had not gone to university.

The research investigates the lifetime financial returns to starting a full-time undergraduate degree at a UK university before the age of 21. The data was produced from analysis of a cohort of England-domiciled students who were born in the mid 1980s and took their GCSE exams in 2002.

More recent data on graduate outcomes was published by the DfE on the 2022-2023 tax year.

The DfE said the government had outlined plans to draw up options to limit the growth of some courses at some providers, where there are consistently "poor returns for students".

The government will begin a new consultation in the autumn to look at options for a minimum English language requirement for prospective undergrads to access student finance.

Minister for Skills Jacqui Smith said it was important that prospective undergrads "choose carefully".

title.en: At least 32 dead, 700 injured as buildings collapse after powerful earthquakes hit Venezuela
title.zh: 委内瑞拉发生强烈地震，建筑物倒塌，恐有“大量人员伤亡”

summary.en: Powerful earthquakes have struck Venezuela, causing buildings to collapse and raising fears of significant casualties. Local authorities are coordinating rescue efforts as homes have been destroyed.
summary.zh: 委内瑞拉发生强烈地震，导致建筑物倒塌，并引发对大量人员伤亡的担忧。地方当局已确认有房屋倒塌，救援工作正在进行中。

body.en:
Powerful twin earthquakes that shook Venezuela killed at least 32 people and injured more than 700, interim president Delcy Rodriguez said on Thursday.

"At this time, we have received reports of 32 deaths" and "more than 700 injured," Rodriguez said in an address to the nation, adding she did not yet have data on the "hardest-hit region" of La Guaira, located near the capital.

The strong earthquakes struck west of Venezuela's capital on Thursday, bringing down buildings in Caracas, trapping people in the rubble.

A magnitude 7.2 earthquake hit about 160km west of Caracas, followed less than a minute later by a magnitude 7.5 tremor, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS).

"High casualties and extensive damage are probable and the disaster is likely widespread," the USGS said, initially estimating the number of people killed would most likely range from 10,000 to 100,000.

Authorities did not immediately provide a national toll for deaths or injuries, but local officials and witnesses reported collapsed buildings, rescues and a growing number of injured.

"We have buildings, homes and houses which have collapsed and we are taking care of things with everything we have available in terms of security, civil assistance," interior minister Diosdado Cabello said on state television. "The fire department, police all have been activated."

Video footage showed emergency workers climbing through the ruins of a collapsed building in the capital as night fell, while distraught relatives sought help for loved ones believed to be trapped.

In Chacao, an eastern Caracas municipality, mayor Gustavo Duque told broadcaster Globovision that two structures had collapsed, 16 people were injured and there were deaths, though he gave no figure for fatalities.

"We're going to do everything we can to rescue the most people possible," he said.

Fire trucks were seen on the streets of Caracas, where some buildings suffered significant facade damage.

At Caracas' Hospital de Clinicas, staff were asked to double up on the night shift to help treat the injured, a worker there said. Video filmed at the hospital showed a darkened hallway with ceiling panels hanging by cables and pieces of plaster scattered across the floor.

Other videos on social media appeared to show significant damage at Venezuela's main airport, while residents reported collapsed buildings in La Guaira, a coastal city near Caracas. Reuters could not immediately verify the footage from the airport and La Guaira.

Some municipalities of Caracas cancelled classes and local events as authorities began to take stock of the damage.

body.en:
All six of today's World Cup matches have wrapped up, with co-hosts Canada and Mexico securing spots in the knockout rounds. Canada and South Africa will move through for the first time ever. Haiti delivered a performance to remember in their final game at the tournament.

South Africa held South Korea off for a 1-0 win, despite serious pressure from the Korean side.

Haiti went down swinging 4-2 to Morocco in their third defeat of the World Cup and their first appearance at the tournament in more than five decades.

Meanwhile, five-time champions Brazil beat Scotland, while Bosnia and Herzegovina wrapped up third in Group B thanks to a 3-1 win over Qatar.

If you're going to watch the match highlights from any of today's games, make it this one.

Co-hosts Mexico cemented top place in World Cup Group A with a perfect record as they defeated the Czech Republic 3-0 on home turf in a deafeningly noisy Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

Despite knowing the win-or-die stakes before them, Czechia never looked a decent shout against a Mexican team borne aloft by a frenzied home crowd.

Mateo Chávez gave Mexico the lead in the 55th minute and Julián Quiñones took advantage of disarray in the Czech defence six minutes later to extend the lead.

Álvaro Fidalgo completed a sparkling evening for the Mexicans as he smashed in a beautiful cross four minutes into added time.

Mexico even brought on goalkeeper Guillermo Ochoa as a second-half substitute, allowing the veteran to play in a sixth World Cup finals at the age of 40. He was lifted and carried by his teammates when the final whistle blew.

The Mexicans have kept a clean sheet in each of their last three World Cup matches. That's a grand total of 315 minutes without a single goal conceded. This is a team that will take some serious work to stop when they're playing at home.

Mexico move on to a last-32 match in the same stadium on 30 June while the Czechs return home after finishing bottom of the group.

South Africa beat South Korea 1-0 to reach the World Cup knockout rounds for the first time in their history — an astonishing turnaround after a dismal opening defeat.

Bafana Bafana, playing at the tournament for the first time since they hosted it in 2010, were widely written off after their 2-0 loss to Group A winners Mexico.

But they battled to a draw against the Czech Republic and came out on top of what was effectively a shootout with South Korea for second place in Monterrey, thanks to Thapelo Maseko's second-half strike.

title.en: France records hottest day on record as Europe swelters through brutal heatwave
title.zh: 法国创下有记录以来最热的一天，欧洲正经历残酷的热浪

summary.en: An estimated 44 million people in France are currently under the highest red alert level for heat.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Europe is struggling to cope with a record-breaking heatwave, with at least 94 million people expected to experience temperatures above 35C, most of them in France and Spain.

Estimates based on analysis of forecasts from the German weather service and 2025 population projections from Europe's Joint Research Centre suggest maximum temperatures will surpass 30C for over 350 million people — more than two-thirds of the continent's population.

The effects of the extreme weather, with temperatures hotter than parts of east and west Africa, have been made worse by buildings and infrastructure not designed to cope with high temperatures.

A scientific study published this week said the current heatwave was "significantly exacerbated by human-induced climate change", without which the current temperatures would have been 2C to 4C cooler.

At a care home on the edge of London, elderly residents struggled to keep cool as the UK recorded its highest ever June temperature of 36.1C.

"We have to find means and ways to protect ourselves and do whatever nature wants. Nature is angry with us because we destroy everything," 97-year-old resident Lucine Nazikian said.

The World Health Organization's director-general Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that the heatwave was putting the health of Europeans at risk.

Around 44 million of the nearly 67 million people in France are currently under the highest red alert level for heat, according to an AFP estimate.

On Wednesday, France experienced its hottest day since measurements began in 1947, the national weather agency said, breaking a record set just a day earlier.

The national temperature indicator — an average of daytime and night-time temperatures across 30 stations — reached 30C, Meteo-France said, citing provisional data.

"We insulated the windows, installed ceiling fans... but without air conditioning it's tough," said Manon Langlois, 34, a teacher in the southwestern city of Bordeaux, where the temperature reached 41.8C.

Spain also broke its June heat record, according to the Aemet weather agency, with an average temperature of 28.17C on Tuesday.

Conditions at many schools, offices and factories across the continent have become unbearable as temperatures rise, forcing early closures and employees to work from home.

"I'm practically swimming in my own sweat, which is not pleasant," 25-year-old decorator Aaron Timothy told AFP in London while cooling off in the shade.

In Italy, where 16 cities are under red alert, the advocacy group Greenpeace said it had detected surface temperatures of 80C in the heavily asphalted area around Rome's Termini railway...

title.en: What does British PM's resignation mean for European security?
title.zh: 英国首相辞职对欧洲安全意味着什么？

summary.en: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer has announced his resignation. He was known for his strong support for Ukraine and efforts to forge a new EU-UK defense partnership. His departure raises questions about the future of these key policies.
summary.zh: 英国首相基尔·斯塔默宣布辞职。他以坚定支持乌克兰和致力于建立新的欧盟-英国防务伙伴关系而闻名。他的离任引发了人们对这些关键政策未来走向的疑问。

body.en:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer was widely known for his support of Ukraine and his efforts towards a new EU–UK defense partnership. What will happen to those policies now that Starmer has announced his resignation?

British Prime Minister Keir Starmer , who on Monday announced he would resign, may not have been that popular with his British constituents lately, but he certainly had many friends among the European Union's top politicians.

As European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen reacted to his resignation on Monday , she wrote: "European and Ukrainian security is stronger because of you. Thank you, dear Keir."

French President Emmanuel Macron also expressed gratitude for Starmer's involvement in Europe's "coalition of the willing" for Ukraine, and for revitalizing EU-UK relations.

It was as a supporter of Ukraine in its war against Russia that Starmer really cemented his reputation in Europe. Together with Macron, Starmer was a leader of the so-called "coalition of the willing." The alliance of 35 states supports Ukraine with military aid and, should there be a ceasefire, would then help Ukraine with longer-term defense.

On social media platform X, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also wrote of his gratitude to Starmer. 

Starmer was a very active and reliable partner within the "coalition of the willing," confirms Olivia O'Sullivan, director of the UK in the World program at British think tank, Chatham House.

O'Sullivan notes that Starmer worked with other leaders to consider how Europe could play a strategic role in securing peace even though he struggled to find the funds needed to meet his self-imposed military spending targets. But that's a challenge that the next British prime minister is also going to face, she points out.

Britain also played a major role advocating for Ukraine within what is known as the E3 format. This framework includes Germany, France and the UK and is supposed to help coordinate the foreign and security policy of all three.

O'Sullivan says the E3 is behind a lot of European strategy, not only regarding Ukraine but also in dealing with the US government, which is increasingly playing a less significant and also less predictable role in European security.

For example, the E3 format has been used to make statements in response to US demands on how Europeans should contribute to securing the Strait of Hormuz.

The fact that the Europeans will now need to adapt to a new British prime minister isn't too much of a setback, O'Sullivan says, although Starmer's departure might see some loss of momentum for the E3.

title.en: Iran after the war — fragile peace, shattered economy
title.zh: 伊朗战后——脆弱的和平，破碎的经济

summary.en: The US has temporarily allowed Iran to export oil and indicated it will provide billions to relieve the crisis triggered by the war. With ordinary Iranians at their limit, however, Tehran already fears new protests.
summary.zh: 美国已暂时允许伊朗出口石油，并表示将提供数十亿美元以缓解战后引发的危机。然而，由于普通伊朗民众已达到极限，德黑兰政府已担心新的抗议活动。

body.en:
The US has temporarily allowed Iran to export oil and indicated it will provide billions to relieve the crisis triggered by the war. With ordinary Iranians at their limit, however, Tehran already fears new protests.

As Washington and Tehran negotiate the implementation of an interim peace deal that ended the Iran war , the US has lifted restrictions on Iranian oil trade until August 21.

The sanctions relief is a central pillar of the peace framework that the two sides signed last week .

At the same time, the US and Qatar are looking into the release of around $6 billion (around €5.3 billion) from frozen Iranian oil revenues. According to US President Donald Trump , the money will be "used for the purchase of food and medical supplies, exclusively from the United States, including Corn, Wheat, and Soybeans from our great American farmers. These are things that are desperately needed by Iran."

But it is clear that Iran badly needs the money — according to preliminary estimates by the Iranian government, the war with the US and Israel caused around €229 billion in damages.

The Memorandum of Understanding between Iran and the US also mentions a $300 billion payout for reconstruction, but the details on that remain unclear.

Iran's government has already been forced to borrow large amounts of money from the central bank in order to cover war expenses, according to Iran's Economy and Finance Minister Seyed Ali Madanizedah.

"An agreement with the US will not fully normalize the Iranian economy,"  said Madanizedah, who got his PhD from the University of Chicago.

Economy expert Ahmad Alavi does not expect any noticeable short-term improvements. Talking to DW, Alavi pointed to the now-defunct JCPOA deal from over a decade ago — increased oil revenues and lower outside pressure kept Iran's economy on "life support," but without deep structural reforms, the effects remained limited and short-lived.

The roots of Iran's economic crisis reach deep into years of sanctions, mismanagement and corruption. On top of that, the war and the recent US blockade of Iranian ports have made the situation even worse.

The crisis is most noticeable in grocery shops — a carton of 15 eggs that used to cost 70,000 toman (€0.37, $0.40) just a year ago is now at over 200,000 toman. Prices of cooking oil and imported rice have also gone up sharply.

"The prices are rising literally every day," a 28-year-old Iranian told DW. "My husband and I both work and we have a small child. We still need to give up so many things. I don't think the prices are ever coming down again."

body.zh: 美国暂时允许伊朗出口石油，并表示将提供数十亿美元来缓解战争引发的危机。然而，由于普通伊朗人已经处于极限，德黑兰已经担心会出现新的抗议活动。 随着华盛顿和德黑兰就结束伊朗战争的临时和平协议进行谈判，美国取消了对伊朗石油贸易的限制，直至 8 月 21 日。 解除制裁是双方上周签署的和平框架的核心支柱。 与此同时，美国和卡塔尔正在考虑从伊朗冻结的石油收入中释放约 60 亿美元（约 53 亿欧元）。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，这笔钱将“用于购买完全来自美国的食品和医疗用品，包括来自我们伟大的美国农民的玉米、小麦和大豆。这些都是伊朗迫切需要的东西。” 但很明显，伊朗急需这笔钱——根据伊朗政府的初步估计，与美国和以色列的战争造成了约2290亿欧元的损失。 伊朗和美国之间的谅解备忘录也提到了3000亿美元的重建费用，但具体细节仍不清楚。 伊朗经济和财政部长赛义德·阿里·马达尼泽表示，伊朗政府已经被迫从中央银行借入大量资金来支付战争费用。 “与美国达成协议不会使伊朗经济完全正常化，”从芝加哥大学获得博士学位的马达尼达说。 经济专家艾哈迈德·阿拉维预计短期内不会出现任何明显的改善。阿拉维在接受德国之声采访时指出，十多年前的联合全面行动计划（JCPOA）现已失效——石油收入的增加和外部压力的降低使伊朗经济得以“维持生命”，但如果不进行深入的结构性改革，其影响仍然有限且短暂。 伊朗经济危机的根源在于多年的制裁、管理不善和腐败。最重要的是，战争和美国最近对伊朗港口的封锁使情况变得更加糟糕。 这场危机在杂货店最为明显——一年前一盒 15 个鸡蛋的售价为 70,000 托曼（0.37 欧元，0.40 美元），现在价格超过 200,000 托曼。食用油和进口大米的价格也大幅上涨。 一名28岁的伊朗人告诉德国之声：“价格几乎每天都在上涨。” “我和我丈夫都工作，我们还有一个小孩。我们仍然需要放弃很多东西。我认为价格不会再下降。” 据伊朗新闻媒体 Tabnak 报道，美元汇率目前约为 1 美元兑换 150,000 托曼。这标志着较近期的利率明显下降......

title.en: Is xenophobia in South Africa risking investment?
title.zh: 南非的仇外心理是否会给投资带来风险？

summary.en: Vigilante groups and right-wing populist forces are stoking anti-immigrant sentiment and demanding that they leave the country by June 30. Experts fear serious economic implications for the country and the region.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Vigilante groups and right-wing populist forces are stoking anti-immigrant sentiment and demanding that they leave the country by June 30. Experts fear serious economic implications for the country and the region.

In South Africa , hostility toward foreigners has flared repeatedly  for decades. Now, protests against irregular migration have turned increasingly violent in multiple cities, driven by right-wing movements and vigilante groups demanding that undocumented migrants leave by June 30. Fears of escalation are rising.

Jo Veary, co-director of the African Center for Migration & Society at the University of the Witwatersrand, links radical protest groups to right-wing populist parties such as ActionSA, which she says are backing them.

Groups like "March and March" and " Operation Dudula " are central. Veary also points to ties with former President Jacob Zuma's MK Party. "They blame foreign residents for the shortcomings in the country's social services. Ultimately, it's about gaining political support and votes in the elections," Veary told DW.

With local elections due in November 2026 , tensions are high. "What we are currently witnessing is a government crisis in South Africa, in which foreigners are being made scapegoats and held responsible for the state's failure to fulfill its duties and promises," she stated, highlighting inequality and unemployment.

Yet migrants play a significant economic role. Foreign investors and entrepreneurs contribute to jobs, trade and industry. Zimbabwean telecoms entrepreneur Strive Masiyiwa's Cassava Technologies is partnering with Nvidia to build Africa's first Artificial Intelligence (AI) factory. Angola's state-run oil giant Sonangol, Mozambique's Matola Gas Company and Nigeria's  Dangote Group are also active across energy and manufacturing.

Many South Africans benefit from these businesses. Still, a 2025 Afrobarometer survey found that 69% believe immigrants harm the economy, despite estimates that each migrant creates about two jobs.

"Even if all foreigners were deported from the country — they make up only about 4% of South Africa's total population (65 million) — this would not suddenly lead to job creation or solve these larger structural problems for which the South African government is responsible," Vearey said.

United States President Donald Trump has said Iran had agreed to nuclear inspections into "infinity", while Iran said it had made no such concession in negotiations, raising questions about the viability of their fragile peace deal.

The two countries, which held a first round of negotiations in Switzerland that ended on Monday, also offered conflicting accounts about financial incentives for Iran, control of the Strait of Hormuz, and Israel's parallel war in Lebanon — all major aspects of the framework deal they signed last week that aims to end the war.

In a sign of easing tensions, the US relaxed travel restrictions on Iran's World Cup football team , allowing the squad to travel from Tijuana, Mexico, to Seattle two days before its next match instead of one.

The Republican-controlled Senate, meanwhile, defied Trump and voted to halt the war, in a largely symbolic move that highlighted fissures in his party.

Though prospects for a lasting peace are far from certain, the initial agreement has allowed traffic to flow again through the Strait of Hormuz, which typically handles one-fifth of global oil supply.

Oil prices on Tuesday were at their lowest level since before the war started on 28 February, and the United Nations' shipping agency said it was working to evacuate 11,000 seafarers stranded when Iran closed the strategic waterway.

The agreement calls for Iran to allow traffic to flow freely for 60 days, but Iran has said it might impose tolls or other fees on shipping after that point.

Iran and Oman, which controls the other side of the strait, issued a joint statement on Tuesday stressing their "sovereign rights" in the waterway and saying they would work together to manage traffic, along with associated costs.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio, visiting Gulf allies unsettled by the peace deal, said Iran would not be allowed to charge tolls in the strait as part of any final agreement.

The deal calls for an immediate end to the war, including in Lebanon, lifting US sanctions on Iran and unfreezing Iranian assets held abroad. It also outlines a US$300 billion ($434 billion) investment fund for the Islamic Republic's reconstruction.

The framework itself imposes no limits on Iran's nuclear program, a subject to be tackled in 60 days of negotiations.

Trump claimed that Iran had agreed to allow international inspectors indefinite access to its damaged nuclear sites.

title.en: Southeast Asia boost defense ties but avoids firm alliances
title.zh: 东南亚加强防务关系但避免建立牢固联盟

summary.en: Countries across the region are expanding defense cooperation in ways that change the South China Sea equation but fall short of a new anti-China bloc.
summary.zh: 东南亚各国正在扩大防务合作，这改变了南海局势，但尚未形成新的反华联盟。

body.en:
Countries across the region are expanding defense cooperation in ways that change the South China Sea equation but fall short of a new anti-China bloc.

For years, the South China Sea has been seen as a potential flashpoint in the intensifying geopolitical rivalry between China and the United States.   

Southeast Asian states are often presented as the smaller powers caught in the storm.

That picture is changing, however, as a new and subtle security network takes shape across the region.

It's built not around formal alliances but around access deals, missile sales, coast guard drills, intelligence-sharing talks and defense consultations.

On June 1, the Philippines and Vietnam upgraded ties to an enhanced strategic partnership and signed a memorandum on defense cooperation which commits them to high-level exchanges, strategic dialogue, information sharing and joint activities at sea.

The partnership builds on earlier coast guard arrangements, including a hotline and mechanisms to prevent incidents.

Late last month, Indian officials said that New Delhi had signed a $629 million (€555 million) deal to supply Vietnam with the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system.

Vietnam is the second Southeast Asian buyer publicly confirmed by India, after the Philippines, which signed a $375 million contract in 2022 for three BrahMos batteries. The missiles are jointly developed by India and Russia.

Meanwhile, Japan's security relationship with the Philippines has grown quite concrete.   A Reciprocal Access Agreement entered into force last September , expanding troop deployment in each country, while this month they began talks over a new deal to share classified defense information.

In February, Australia and Indonesia signed the "Jakarta Treaty," a common security pact that commits the two governments to regular top-level consultations.

None of these agreements creates a NATO-style alliance . Together, however, they show how middle powers are trying to make unilateral pressure at sea harder and costlier.

All these countries share concerns about China and an interest in upholding the rule of law at sea and keeping the region free from coercion by great powers, Hunter Marston, director of the Southeast Asia Program at the Lowy Institute, told DW.

At the same time, they recognize — to varying degrees — the possibility that the US could scale back its commitments to regional security, which would introduce volatility and unpredictability into the prevailing balance of power, he said.

"While they don't all see eye to eye on regional security or support the United States military presence equally, now is the time for middle powers to band together to stand up for their interests. None are strong enough to do so...
body.zh: 该地区各国正在扩大防务合作，其方式改变了南海局势，但并未形成新的反华集团。 多年来，南海一直被视为中美地缘政治竞争的潜在爆发点。 东南亚国家经常被描述为陷入风暴的小国。 然而，随着整个地区新的、微妙的安全网络的形成，这种情况正在发生变化。 它不是围绕正式联盟建立的，而是围绕准入协议、导弹销售、海岸警卫队演习、情报共享会谈和国防磋商建立的。 6 月 1 日，菲律宾和越南将关系提升为强化战略伙伴关系，并签署了一份防务合作备忘录，承诺两国进行高层交往、战略对话、信息共享和海上联合活动。 该伙伴关系建立在早期海岸警卫队安排的基础上，包括热线电话和预防事件的机制。 上个月末，印度官员表示，新德里已签署一项价值 6.29 亿美元（5.55 亿欧元）的协议，向越南提供布拉莫斯超音速巡航导弹系统。 越南是继菲律宾之后印度公开确认的第二个东南亚买家，菲律宾于2022年签署了价值3.75亿美元的三块布拉莫斯电池合同。该导弹由印度和俄罗斯联合研制。 与此同时，日本与菲律宾的安全关系变得相当具体。 去年九月，一项互惠访问协议生效，扩大了两国的部队部署，本月他们开始就一项共享机密国防信息的新协议进行谈判。 今年二月，澳大利亚和印度尼西亚签署了《雅加达条约》，这是一项共同安全条约，要求两国政府定期进行高层磋商。 这些协议都没有创建北约式的联盟。然而，它们共同表明中等强国如何试图加大海上单边施压的难度和成本。 洛伊研究所东南亚项目主任亨特·马斯顿告诉德国之声，所有这些国家都对中国感到担忧，都对维护海上法治和使该地区免受大国胁迫感兴趣。 他表示，与此同时，他们在不同程度上认识到美国可能缩减其对地区安全的承诺，这将给当前的均势带来波动和不可预测性。 “虽然他们在地区安全问题上意见不一，也并不平等地支持美国的军事存在，但现在是中等强国联合起来维护自身利益的时候了。没有一个国家足够强大，可以这样做……

summary.en: South Korea's military is investigating why a North Korean soldier crossed the heavily fortified inner-Korean border, a rare event given that most North Koreans who flee usually do so via China.
summary.zh: 韩国军方正在调查一名朝鲜士兵越过朝韩边境的原因。虽然每年有数十名朝鲜人逃离，通常经由中国，但直接向南越境的情况非常罕见。

body.zh: 韩国军方表示，正在调查这名士兵越过朝韩边境的原因。虽然每年都有数十名朝鲜人逃离（通常经由中国），但直接越境南下的情况却非常罕见。 韩国军方周三表示，一名朝鲜士兵在越过朝韩边界中部附近地区后被拘留了一夜。 首尔参谋长联席会议在给包括韩联社在内的媒体的消息中表示，“周二晚间，军方在中央前线抓获了一名朝鲜士兵，有关当局目前正在调查细节。” 韩国联合通讯社也报道称，这名士兵据信希望叛逃，但未援引消息来源。 朝鲜和韩国被戒备森严的边界隔开，边界两侧都有一个称为非军事区的特殊分界区，之后还有二级缓冲区。 尽管自 20 世纪 50 年代朝鲜半岛因战争分裂以来，已有数万名朝鲜人逃往南方，但他们通常通过陆路向北逃往邻国中国。他们往往从那里进入第三国，例如泰国，然后最终前往南方。 2024 年，即韩国统一部公布数据的最后一年，有 236 名朝鲜人抵达韩国。 不过，跨越陆地边界的叛逃情况非常罕见。边境的大部分地区森林茂密，境内布满地雷，两国军队都在各自的边境严密监视。 韩联社报道称，这是 2026 年首例此类案例。 据称，自去年六月李在明政府上台以来，已登记了四起案件。据韩联社报道，其中两次发生在 7 月，最近一次发生在 10 月。 新来者往往会被移交给情报部门进行安全检查。 一旦这一过程完成，韩国通常会授予脱北者公民身份，朝鲜认为这种做法是一种侮辱。它经常以非常严厉的措辞谈论叛逃者。 1950-53 年朝鲜战争之后，两国在技术上仍处于冻结战争状态，只签署了停战协议，没有签署和平协议。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间将我们选为 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

Deuteronomy 10:19 reminds us to love the foreigner, recalling that Yahweh's people once experienced displacement and vulnerability. This calls us to compassion and understanding for those who seek refuge across divides.

verse.textZh: 所以你们要怜爱寄居的，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: China detains two Japanese nationals on smuggling charges
title.zh: 中国以走私罪拘留两名日本公民

summary.en: China has detained two Japanese nationals on suspicion of smuggling banned goods. Reports suggest that at least one case may involve strategic rare-earth-related exports.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
China has detained two Japanese nationals on suspicion of smuggling banned goods. Reports suggest that at least one case may involve strategic rare-earth-related exports.

China has detained two Japanese nationals on suspicion of smuggling banned goods, Tokyo said on Wednesday.

Japanese media reported that one case may involve rare-earth-related exports, a strategically important sector tightly controlled by Beijing .

Japan said Chinese authorities informed it that one citizen was detained in the northeastern port city of Dalian on May 18 on suspicion of violating a law covering the smuggling of goods banned from trade.

A second Japanese national was detained on the same allegation on May 25, Japan's top government spokesperson, Minoru Kihara, told reporters.

"The [Japanese government] will continue taking appropriate steps to protect Japanese citizens," Kihara said.

China's Foreign Ministry confirmed the detentions, saying the two Japanese citizens had violated Chinese law, but provided no further details.

"We would like to stress that Japan should educate and remind its citizens and businesses in China to abide by Chinese laws and regulations," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said.

Japanese media reported that one of the cases involved allegations of attempts to export products containing rare earth materials, which are subject to Chinese restrictions. Kihara did not identify the goods involved.

"These cases remain under investigation," a spokesperson from Japan's consular offices in China told the AFP news agency. He added that the two individuals appeared to be in good health and that the government would "take appropriate measures from the standpoint of their protection."

China dominates global production and processing of rare earths , metals which are used in products ranging from electric vehicles to military equipment. Beijing has tightened controls on the sector in recent years and increasingly views it as a strategic asset.

Relations between Japan and China have deteriorated since comments by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi last year suggesting Tokyo could intervene militarily if China attempted to seize Taiwan.

Since then, China has restricted exports of some key minerals and dual-use goods to Japan, while also scaling back a range of trade and cultural exchanges.

body.zh: 中国以涉嫌走私违禁品为由拘留了两名日本公民。报告显示，至少有一起案件可能涉及战略性稀土相关出口。 东京周三表示，中国因涉嫌走私违禁物品而拘留了两名日本公民。 日本媒体报道称，其中一起案件可能涉及稀土相关出口，这是一个受到北京严格控制的具有重要战略意义的行业。 日本表示，中国当局通知其，一名公民于 5 月 18 日在东北港口城市大连因涉嫌违反走私禁止贸易货物的法律而被拘留。 日本政府最高发言人 Minoru Kihara 告诉记者，5 月 25 日，第二名日本公民因同一指控被拘留。 “[日本政府]将继续采取适当措施保护日本公民，”木原说。 中国外交部证实了拘留事件，称这两名日本公民违反了中国法律，但没有提供更多细节。 外交部发言人郭家琨表示，我们要强调，日方应教育、提醒在华公民和企业遵守中国法律法规。 日本媒体报道称，其中一起案件涉及指控试图出口含有稀土材料的产品，而这些产品受到中国的限制。木原没有透露涉案商品的名称。 日本驻华领事办公室发言人告诉法新社：“这些案件仍在调查中。”他补充说，这两个人似乎健康状况良好，政府将“从保护他们的角度采取适当措施”。 中国主导着全球稀土和金属的生产和加工，这些金属用于从电动汽车到军事设备等各种产品。近年来，北京加强了对该行业的控制，并越来越将其视为战略资产。 自从日本首相高市早苗去年发表言论暗示如果中国试图夺取台湾，日本可能会进行军事干预以来，日本和中国之间的关系已经恶化。 此后，中国限制了一些关键矿产和军民两用商品向日本的出口，同时还缩减了一系列贸易和文化交流。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间点击此处并点击“星标”或“首选”按钮，将我们选为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

title.en: Dear You review – enjoyable Chinese romdram crosses generations as it tracks down a missing husband
title.zh: 《亲爱的你》影评：一部跨越世代、追寻失踪丈夫的感人华语爱情剧情片

summary.en: The Guardian China reviews "Dear You," a Chinese romantic drama by director Lan Hongchun. The film is a multi-generational family saga, spanning from the 1940s to the present, primarily set in Bangkok, and follows the search for a husband who disappeared in Thailand.
summary.zh: 《卫报中国》评论了导演蓝鸿春的华语爱情剧情片《亲爱的你》。这部电影是一部跨越几代人的家族传奇，故事从20世纪40年代至今，主要背景设在曼谷，讲述了一个家庭寻找在泰国失踪的丈夫的故事。

body.en: Director Lan Hongchun’s family saga feels like a good old-fashioned novel as it goes in search of a man who has disappeared in Thailand With a story that ranges from the 1940s to the present and, although mostly set in Bangkok, revolving largely around Teochew-speaking Chinese from Guangdong, this generations-spanning drama feels like a good old-fashioned novel. A romantic beach read, perhaps, the kind in which coincidences and random accidents cause misunderstandings that last for decades until the truth is finally revealed. It’s sentimental in places, sure, but there’s also a fair bit of salty, bawdy humour to cut the sweetness, lashings of period colour, and impressively naturalistic performances from a mostly non-professional cast. All that has helped to make this an unexpectedly large box-office hit in the People’s Republic last month; and for non-Chinese or Thai rom-dram aficionados anywhere, it’s well worth looking out for. As the story opens in the 21st century in the Chinese city of Shantou, octogenarian Shurou (Iap Sok-jiu) is celebrating her 87th birthday, surrounded by adoring friends, family and neighbours who revere the matriarch, not least for managing to raise three kids on her own in the 1940s and 50s. Her shifty grandson Xiaowei (Hiau-ui), however, is less of a solid citizen and, having got into debt, he decides to travel to Bangkok to find out if Shurou’s husband Zheng Musheng, not seen for decades, could help out since he’s reputed to have made a fortune out there, endowed schools all over Thailand, and had a second family after abandoning Shurou. Continue reading...
body.zh: 导演兰鸿春的家庭传奇感觉就像一部优秀的老式小说，讲述了在泰国寻找失踪男子的故事。故事范围从 20 世纪 40 年代至今，虽然主要以曼谷为背景，但主要围绕来自广东的潮州华人展开，这部跨越几代人的戏剧感觉就像一部优秀的老式小说。浪漫的海滩读物，也许是那种巧合和偶然的事故会导致持续数十年的误会，直到真相最终揭晓的类型。当然，它在某些地方是感伤的，但也有一些咸味、下流的幽默来削弱甜蜜，充满时代色彩，以及来自大多数非专业演员的令人印象深刻的自然主义表演。所有这些都使得该片上个月在中华人民共和国取得了意想不到的票房大成功。对于任何地方的非中国或泰国的浪漫剧爱好者来说，这都非常值得一看。故事发生在 21 世纪的中国汕头市，八十多岁的淑柔（叶淑如饰）正在庆祝她的 87 岁生日，周围都是崇拜这位女族长的朋友、家人和邻居，尤其是她在 20 世纪 40 年代和 50 年代设法独自抚养三个孩子。然而，她狡猾的孙子小伟（孝仪饰）却不是一个踏实的公民，负债累累，他决定前往曼谷，看看书柔数十年未见的丈夫郑木胜是否可以帮忙，因为他在外面发了大财，为泰国各地的学校捐款，并在抛弃书柔后有了第二个家庭。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The multi-generational search for a missing husband in "Dear You" powerfully illustrates the enduring nature of family bonds. This long quest reflects the deep commitment inherent in marriage, where two become one, a union that transcends time and distance. It reminds us that true connection often calls for steadfastness, even in the face of profound...
reflection.zh: 电影《亲爱的你》中跨越几代人寻找失踪丈夫的故事，有力地展现了家庭纽带的持久性。这场漫长的寻觅反映了婚姻中固有的深刻承诺，夫妻二人成为一体，这种结合超越了时间和距离。它提醒我们，真正的连接往往需要坚韧不拔，即使面对巨大的不确定性也是如此。

verse.textEn: That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife, and they become one flesh.
verse.textZh: 因此，人要离开父母，与妻子连合，二人成为一体。

body.en: British disinfectant brand withdraws advert about a man’s efforts to find a ‘clean and untouched’ woman The British hygiene brand Dettol has apologised after an advertisement released in China, which it said was intended to criticise “toxic men”, was widely condemned on social media as offensive to women. The five-minute advert for a multipurpose disinfectant, released across many online platforms at the end of May, features a man comparing his girlfriend with his former partner. Learning that his former girlfriend previously lived with someone else, the man likens their relationship to a “secondhand service”. He then tells his friends that he intends to find a “clean and untouched” woman for whom he can be the first sexual partner. Continue reading...

title.en: Chinese supercomputer leapfrogs best US machines to be ranked world’s fastest
title.zh: 中国超级计算机超越美国机器，位居世界第一

summary.en: China's LineShine supercomputer has been ranked the world's fastest, surpassing its US counterparts. This marks the first time since 2017 that a Chinese machine has topped the Top500 list, which is often seen as a measure of national technological prowess.
summary.zh: 中国的“神威·太湖之光”超级计算机被评为全球最快，超越了美国同类机器。这是自2017年以来，中国计算机首次登上全球超级计算机500强榜首，该榜单常被视为衡量国家科技实力的指标。

body.en: China’s LineShine debuts at number one in Top500 – a list sometimes viewed as a national measure of global tech prowess A supercomputer in China now outranks its US counterparts as the world’s most powerful. It is the first time since 2017 that a Chinese computer has topped a list sometimes viewed as a measure of a nation’s technological prowess. The LineShine computer in Shenzhen displaced top-ranked US computer El Capitan in the Top500 rankings released on Tuesday. It was LineShine’s debut on the list. Continue reading...

This technological milestone reminds us of the prophetic words that in the end times, knowledge shall increase. It prompts reflection on how we steward such immense intellectual and computational power.
reflection.zh: 世界最快超级计算机的新闻，凸显了人类对知识不懈的追求和加速。这一技术里程碑提醒我们，在末时知识必会增长的预言。它促使我们思考如何管理如此巨大的智力和计算能力。

title.en: Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher Jimmy Lai honored by DW
title.zh: 香港亲民主派出版商黎智英获德国之声表彰

summary.en: Jimmy Lai, a Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher, has been honored by DW. He founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper before being sentenced to 20 years in prison. His son stated that the award signifies that those who advocate for the freedom of others are not alone.
summary.zh: 香港亲民主派出版商黎智英获得德国之声表彰。他在被判处20年监禁前，创办了香港最大的亲民主报纸。他的儿子表示，这个奖项表明那些为他人自由而奋斗的人“从不孤单”。

body.en:
Before being imprisoned for 20 years, Jimmy Lai founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper. His son said the award shows that those who fight for the freedom of others "are never alone."

Arriving in Hong Kong as a penniless 12-year-old stowaway from southern China, Jimmy Lai sought only freedom and a future. At the time, Lai could never have imagined how his life would become forever intertwined with this former British colony.

"I'll sink with the ship, because this place gives me everything," said Lai in an interview about Hong Kong with DW a few months before he was taken into custody in December 2020. He was one of the first high-profile figures to be targeted under a "national security law" imposed on Hong Kong by Beijing following a crackdown on pro-democracy protests.

Beijing had said the law would restore Hong Kong "from chaos to order" after demonstrations in 2019 opposing an extradition bill morphed into massive protests against Beijing encroaching on Hong Kong's civil liberties .

Since then, the pro-democracy media mogul has spent more than 2,000 days in solitary confinement in Hong Kong's maximum-security Stanley Prison.

Lai's years-long trial ended this February, when the 78-year-old was sentenced to 20 years in prison for "colluding with foreign forces." While he had pleaded not guilty to all charges, his legal team said he will not appeal.

The sentence is the heaviest punishment handed down so far under the national security law, and Lai's trial has symbolized for many people the severe erosion of press freedom in Hong Kong as part of Beijing's broader strategy to silence critical voices.

In recognition of his defense of press freedom and freedom of speech, DW honored Jimmy Lai with this year's Freedom of Speech Award  at the annual Global Media Forum in Bonn, Germany, on Tuesday.

"While we have spoken freely in the defence of independent media, Jimmy, who founded an independent media company because he believed in the rights of the Hong Kong people to receive information, is locked away for those beliefs," Jodie Ginsberg, CEO of the Committee to Protect Journalists, said in a speech honoring Lai.

"The attacks on Apple Daily and its counterparts in Hong Kong presaged the far greater attacks on civil liberties in the years that followed. Jimmy Lai saw this and spoke out. We can honor him today not only by fighting for his freedom, but by defending the freedoms for which he was jailed."

Since 2015, the DW Freedom of Speech Award has honored journalists and human rights defenders as a way to call attention to restrictions on press freedom and concerning human rights situations around the world.

summary.en: Electric vehicles are becoming more affordable, efficient, and capable of longer distances, exceeding initial growth forecasts. China is leading this transition, with Europe and other nations rapidly advancing as well.

body.zh: 电动汽车变得越来越便宜、越来越高效，而且行驶距离比以往任何时候都更远。中国正在推动这一转型，但欧洲和其他国家正在快速追赶。 全球电动汽车 (EV) 市场的增长速度远远快于预期。短短六年内，销量增长了十倍，到 2025 年，全球电动汽车销量将达到约 2100 万辆。 中国和欧洲处于领先地位，但世界其他地区的市场也在快速增长。 中国长期以来一直在投资太阳能和风能以及电池技术——电动汽车最关键的组成部分。 得益于先进的研究和大规模生产，电动汽车电池成本大幅下降。如今，它们的成本仅为 10 年前的四分之一，而且价格还在继续下降。 中国是世界上最大的汽车市场，消费者正在从政府的产业战略中获益。自 2024 年以来，电动汽车的成本低于内燃机汽车，国家多年来一直在迅速扩大充电基础设施，而且中国的电力非常实惠。 2015年，电动汽车仅占中国新车销量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，这一比例已攀升至 61%。 电动汽车依靠电力运行并通过电缆充电。在全球范围内，三分之二的电动汽车是所谓的电池电动汽车 (BEV)，仅由电力驱动。剩下的三分之一还配备了燃气发动机，用于长途旅行时的备用——这些被称为增程电动汽车 (EREV) 或插电式混合动力电动汽车 (PHEV)。 相比之下，所谓的混合动力电动汽车 (HEV) 始终需要汽油或柴油来为其内燃机提供动力。电动机提供一些帮助，仅通过再生制动产生电力。这项技术在一定程度上降低了城市驾驶的燃油消耗，但混合动力汽车在国际统计中并未被算作电动汽车。 2018年，电动汽车仅占欧盟新车注册量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，售出的新车中近三分之一是电动汽车。 北欧处于领先地位。在挪威，现在销售的几乎所有新车都是电动汽车（99%），其次是丹麦（82%）和瑞典（65%）。该地区各国政府支持气候友好型出行，并正在扩大充电基础设施。 在英国，2026 年 4 月注册的新车中有 39% 是电动汽车，其次是德国（37%）和法国（32%）。在这三个国家，电动汽车销量与去年同月相比都翻了一番。 近年来，美国市场陷入停滞。 2023 年至 2025 年间，电动汽车占...

body.en:
While former teal independents Allegra Spender and Zali Steggall were launching their new political party to voters, many online were focused on something else entirely — its name.

Dubbed Community Strong Australia (CSA), Spender and Steggall say they hope their teal-branded party will become a home for community-backed candidates that offers a centrist alternative to One Nation. Still, online, the name has been roundly criticised by members of the public.

She said the pair had had to avoid "stepping on the toes" of the teal independents who had not yet joined their party, and they had to avoid sounding too much like the 'voices for' political movement.

Speaking to the ABC, Spender said CSA was unlike any party that had come before it because it prioritised community representation above all else.

"That's what people are really asking for, they want politicians to put their communities first, but at the same time people want [politicians] to work collaboratively," she said.

Sheppard said this was a complex vision to shoehorn into a name, given that they needed to take their parliamentary colleagues into account.

"You're trying to build a brand from nothing, and you're trying to not step on the toes of people that you've been working with over the last two terms of Parliament," she said.

"That leaves them with not too many places to go, but they really obviously want to emphasise this community aspect."

The party has no leader and will give its members a 'free vote', meaning they can vote issue by issue in line with what their constituents want them to.

A political party would likely be able to manage campaigning resources differently and support multiple candidates, as opposed to independents.

In a statement to SBS News, CSA said the "strength of the country is based on the strength of our communities."

"Community Strong has come out of the community and will build on achievements of community independents to give Australians an alternative to the two-party system that has let them down."

Sheppard said the new party was trying to differentiate itself while also squeezing into a very small spot "on the political map."

"There's obviously an electorate out there for a centrist party that cares about the environment, but it's not a huge part of the electorate, and I think their name reflects how difficult that is."

body.en:
Big changes to how Australians benefit from their investments and pay tax have passed through federal parliament following a last-minute deal with the Greens.

The reforms, first unveiled in the May budget , include changes to capital gains tax, negative gearing and income tax.

These changes — along with a few tweaks — have now become law. Here's everything you need to know.

Despite announcing the changes in its May budget, Labor's minority position in the Senate meant they needed nine votes from the crossbench to pass its new tax bill.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

On Tuesday, the Greens agreed to give Labor their 10 votes in exchange for several key amendments to the bill and an eight-week delay on the federal government's plans to overhaul the NDIS .

The minor party also agreed to support the tax changes after the government said it would remove a loophole that allowed investors with self-managed super funds (SMSFs) to borrow money to buy housing.

Super funds aren't generally allowed to borrow for investments, but the loophole allowed SMSFs to borrow money to buy single assets like property if their loans were set up in certain ways.

These loans account for 1 per cent of all mortgages at the moment, but the Greens said this change would stop people flocking to SMSFs now that it has become harder to invest in property.

The Greens also negotiated for Labor to drop a clause in the bill that would have allowed the government to reverse the reforms in the future.

Under the new legislation, effective from 1 July 2027, investors will no longer qualify for the 50 per cent capital gains tax (CGT) discount on profits from the sale of assets.

Instead, profits on sold assets — that is, capital gains — will be replaced by a cost-based indexation and a minimum 30 per cent tax rate.

Earlier this month, the government announced it was investigating a carve-out for startup founders, employees who receive shares, and early investors, recognising the sector's reliance on the potential for significant returns to attract capital and talent.

Businesses earning less than $10 million a year will also still be eligible for a 50 per cent CGT discount.

The new legislation also locks in another cornerstone of the Albanese government's May budget by abolishing negative gearing for established properties.

The changes to negative gearing only apply to homes purchased or under contract before 7.30pm AEST on 12 May 2026.

New builds and some government housing programs will still be eligible for negative gearing.

The legislation also includes key changes to how much tax working Australians will pay in future financial years.

body.en:
Angus Taylor has responded to mounting pressure over his stance on multiculturalism — including from within his own party — after being repeatedly asked whether he rejects One Nation's push for a "monocultural" Australia.

The Opposition leader said he stands by "a version" of multiculturalism that aligns with what he has called Australia's "core values".

He separately pointed to Japan as having a "monoculture" he wouldn't want to replicate.

"We should have a common set of values we all agree on. I mean, we need every Australian to believe in our system of law, to believe in our basic freedoms … our parliamentary democracy," Taylor told Sydney's 2GB radio station on Thursday.

In a separate interview with Channel Nine's Today Show, Taylor said he was unclear on what a monoculture looked like.

"I don't know what monoculture means. I hear, in the last day or so, it's something like looking like Japan. I don't want Australia to look like Japan. I want Australia to look like Australia."

His comments come after One Nation leader Pauline Hanson delivered her first National Press Club address last week. During the speech, Hanson outlined her vision for a "monocultural" society where "Australians must live under the one cultural umbrella".

Some experts have told SBS News that there's "never been a monoculture in Australia".

Hanson has also praised Japan as a monocultural or largely ethnically homogenous society this week. The country is becoming increasingly multicultural due to labour shortages , an ageing population and low birthrates , according to recent research.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has dismissed the idea of a monocultural Australia as "nonsense". However, Taylor's stance has been less clear.

In a press conference on Tuesday, Taylor was asked whether Australia should be a monoculture.

A journalist pressed further, claiming that Taylor had "dodged four questions in a row" about multiculturalism. The Opposition leader responded:

"We can have people from all over the world of all races and religions in this country, but they must share those core values. I don't know how much simpler it can be than that."

On Wednesday, Liberal backbencher Andrew McLachlan called on his leader to, "embrace the reality of modern Australia".

Albanese taunted Taylor over the exchange with reporters during Question Time that day.

"My job isn't to give advice to this bloke, but my advice is how about you stand up to One Nation on something?" Albanese said.

Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke also commented on Taylor's stance on multiculturalism.

One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has offered Karl Stefanovic a job after Nine newspapers reported he would leave the network, following backlash over his interview with far-right figure Tommy Robinson on his podcast — which is independent from Nine.

Nine reportedly decided to cut ties with Stefanovic after the podcast episode was released, and the presenter is negotiating terms of his exit from the network, for which he has co-hosted its flagship morning show, Today, for two decades.

Speaking to Andrew Bolt on Sky News on Wednesday night, Hanson accused Nine of moving to the "left".

"Karl, come and apply for a job with me. We'll have a great time, we'll put them all on notice, and we'll get the country back on track, mate."

Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, is a far-right anti-Islam activist in the United Kingdom, linked to violent anti-immigration riots in the UK and co-founder of the now-defunct anti-Islam group English Defence League.

When Stefanovic first launched his independent podcast in January, he promised to "unleash the beast".

"I have this curious beast inside my head, and I'm about to unleash that beast," he said in the trailer.

His debut episode, featuring a 55-minute interview with Pauline Hanson, sits at over 300,000 views on YouTube.

In the 66 episodes published since, Stefanovic has interviewed guests ranging from the controversial, such as billionaire Clive Palmer, to the expected, such as Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.

However, it was his interview with Tommy Robinson published on Tuesday evening that landed Stefanovic in hot water.

Stefanovic introduced Robinson in the interview as "one of Britain's most controversial figures".

Robinson, a former tanning salon owner turned anti-Islam activist, has been banned from several social media platforms for violating rules on hateful conduct and hate speech and has multiple criminal convictions.

"I really do admire your tenacity and the courage that you're showing in trying to stand up for what you believe is right," Stefanovic told Robinson during the interview.

Stefanovic and Robinson discussed populist politics in the UK, the United States, and elsewhere.

"I love her, Pauline," Robinson said of the One Nation leader, in reference to the connection between the two figures.

"She's been through what I've been through: she's been condemned, attacked, battered, every name under the sun.

Stefanovic and Robinson are seen walking side by side, Robinson wearing a "Unite the Kingdom" T-shirt, the name given to a series of large-scale anti-immigration rallies in London.
